name: Saint Louis Abbey
fact: A Benedictine monastery in Creve Coeur, known for its round church.

name: Ameristar Casino
fact: A casino on the Missouri River in St. Charles, at 1 Ameristar Boulevard.

name: Hollywood Casino Amphitheatre
fact: The big outdoor concert shed at Riverport in Maryland Heights.

name: Anheuser-Busch Brewery
fact: The St. Louis brewery tour, at the Budweiser Brewery Experience beside Pestalozzi Street.

name: Gateway Arch
fact: A 630-foot stainless-steel arch on the riverfront, the tallest arch in the world.

name: Saint Louis Art Museum
fact: The art museum at the top of Art Hill in Forest Park.

name: Babler State Park
fact: A wooded state park in Wildwood, named for Dr. Edmund A. Babler.

name: Jefferson Barracks
fact: The old riverfront military post, now a county park and historic site in Lemay.

name: Bellefontaine Cemetery
fact: Opened in 1849 on the north side. William Clark is buried here.

name: World Bird Sanctuary
fact: A Valley Park center for birds of prey, with eagles and owls on the grounds.

name: Busch Stadium
fact: The Cardinals' downtown ballpark on Clark Avenue, opened in 2006.

name: Butterfly House
fact: The Sophia M. Sachs Butterfly House at Faust Park in Chesterfield.

name: Cahokia Mounds
fact: The great Mississippian city across the river. The pin is the top of Monks Mound.

name: Calvary Cemetery
fact: A Catholic cemetery founded in 1854, resting place of Dred Scott and General Sherman.

name: Carondelet Park
fact: A large south-city park in the Carondelet neighborhood.

name: Castlewood State Park
fact: River bluffs and trails above the Meramec, in Ballwin.

name: Cathedral Basilica
fact: The cathedral on Lindell, completed in 1914, with mosaics covering the interior.

name: Chain of Rocks Bridge
fact: The 1929 Mississippi River bridge with a 22-degree bend, now a walking and bike path.

name: Chase Park Plaza
fact: The grand hotel on Lindell in the Central West End, across from Forest Park.

name: City Museum
fact: A museum of climbs and tunnels built from scrap, in the old International Shoe building.

name: Cliff Cave Park
fact: A county park in Oakville where a cave opens in the bluff above the Mississippi.

name: Columbia Bottom Conservation Area
fact: The conservation area where the Missouri River meets the Mississippi.

name: Compton Hill Water Tower
fact: The stone water tower above Compton Heights, on one of the highest points in the city.

name: Creve Coeur Lake
fact: The sailboat lake and county park in Maryland Heights.

name: Crown Candy Kitchen
fact: Old North's soda fountain, the oldest still running in the metro.

name: Energizer Park
fact: CITY SC's soccer stadium next to Union Station, opened in 2022 as CityPark.

name: Enterprise Center
fact: The downtown arena on Clark Avenue, home of the Blues.

name: Fairground Park
fact: The north-city park on the site of the 19th-century St. Louis fairgrounds.

name: World's Fair Pavilion
fact: The open-air pavilion on Government Drive in the middle of Forest Park.

name: Family Arena
fact: St. Charles's concert and sports arena on Arena Parkway.

name: Fort Belle Fontaine
fact: The first U.S. military fort west of the Mississippi, now a county park on the Missouri River.

name: Gateway Geyser
fact: A fountain in Malcolm W. Martin Memorial Park, aimed back at the Gateway Arch.

name: Grant's Farm
fact: Ulysses S. Grant's old farm in Grantwood Village, later a Busch family animal park.

name: Missouri History Museum
fact: The Missouri History Museum on the north side of Forest Park.

name: Horseshoe Lake State Park
fact: An oxbow-lake state park in the Metro East, near Pontoon Beach.

name: Indian Camp Creek Park
fact: St. Charles County's largest park, 603 acres on Dietrich Road in Foristell.

name: Jewel Box
fact: The Art Deco glass greenhouse in Forest Park, finished in 1936.

name: Scott Joplin House
fact: The Delmar Boulevard house where Scott Joplin lived from 1901 to 1903.

name: Kiener Plaza
fact: The downtown park between Busch Stadium and the Old Courthouse.

name: Lafayette Park
fact: The iron-fenced park in the middle of Lafayette Square.

name: Lambert Airport
fact: Terminal 1 at St. Louis Lambert International Airport.

name: Laumeier Sculpture Park
fact: Sunset Hills' outdoor museum, with more than 70 large sculptures on 105 acres.

name: Lewis and Clark State Historic Site
fact: The Hartford site of Camp River Dubois, the Corps of Discovery's winter camp in 1803.

name: Lone Elk Park
fact: A fenced preserve in Valley Park where a herd of elk roams the hills.

name: Delmar Loop
fact: Delmar's strip of clubs and shops. The pin is Blueberry Hill.

name: The Magic House
fact: Kirkwood's children's museum at 516 South Kirkwood Road.

name: Historic Main Street
fact: The brick blocks of South Main in St. Charles. The pin is the First Missouri State Capitol.

name: Mastodon State Historic Site
fact: A historic site in Imperial where mastodon bones were dug from the Kimmswick clay.

name: Missouri Botanical Garden
fact: The Missouri Botanical Garden in the Shaw neighborhood, home of the Climatron.

name: The Muny
fact: Forest Park's outdoor musical theater, with free seats in the last rows all summer.

name: O'Fallon Park
fact: A north-city park with a lake, named for the landowner John O'Fallon.

name: Powder Valley Nature Center
fact: A Missouri Department of Conservation nature center in the woods of Sunset Hills.

name: Purina Farms
fact: Nestlé Purina's visitor farm on Checkerboard Drive in Gray Summit.

name: Queeny Park
fact: A large St. Louis County park off Weidman Road, named for Edgar Monsanto Queeny.

name: National Great Rivers Museum
fact: The river museum beside Melvin Price Locks and Dam in Alton.

name: Route 66 State Park
fact: A state park on the old Times Beach site, along the Meramec east of Eureka.

name: Saint Louis Science Center
fact: The hands-on science museum on Oakland Avenue, at Forest Park's southeast corner.

name: Schlafly Bottleworks
fact: The Schlafly brewery and beer hall in a Maplewood bottle works.

name: Shaw Park
fact: Clayton's central park, just west of downtown Clayton.

name: Six Flags St. Louis
fact: The Eureka amusement park on Six Flags Road, opened in 1971 as Six Flags Over Mid-America.

name: Saint Louis University
fact: Saint Louis University's midtown campus on Grand Boulevard.

name: Soulard Market
fact: Soulard's public market, the oldest farmers market in the city.

name: Suson Park
fact: A south-county park with a small animal farm you can walk through.

name: Ted Drewes on Chippewa
fact: The Chippewa Street frozen-custard stand on old Route 66. A concrete is thick enough to turn upside down.

name: The Hill
fact: St. Louis's Italian neighborhood. The pin sits on St. Ambrose Church.

name: Tilles Park
fact: Ladue's main park, with trails, a playground, and an outdoor stage.

name: Tower Grove Park
fact: The Victorian park just south of the Botanical Garden, given to the city by Henry Shaw.

name: Museum of Transportation
fact: A rail museum on Barrett Station Road in Kirkwood, full of locomotives.

name: UMSL
fact: The University of Missouri–St. Louis campus on Natural Bridge Road.

name: Union Station
fact: The historic train station on Market Street, now a hotel and entertainment hall.

name: Washington University
fact: Washington University's Danforth campus. The pin is Brookings Hall.

name: Willmore Park
fact: A hilly park in southwest St. Louis, along the River Des Peres.

name: Endangered Wolf Center
fact: A breeding center near Eureka for endangered red wolves and Mexican wolves.

name: Saint Louis Zoo
fact: The Saint Louis Zoo in Forest Park, where general admission is free.
